title: AstroMLab 2: AstroLLaMA-2-70B Model and Benchmarking Specialised LLMs for Astronomy
problem: Astronomy-focused LLM benchmarks are absent, hindering objective evaluation of domain-specialized models. Previous AstroLLaMA series based on LLaMA-2-7B showed performance degradation compared to base models due to catastrophic forgetting.
motivation: Establishing astronomy-specific benchmarks enables quantitative assessment of domain-specialized LLMs and understanding how continual pretraining affects performance in specialized domains.
method: Researchers continued training LLaMA-2 models (7 billion and 70 billion parameters) on astronomy papers from arXiv, then tested the results with astronomy multiple-choice questions. They compared the specialized models against the original base models to see whether high-quality astronomy data prevented catastrophic forgetting—the tendency for models to lose general knowledge when trained on a specific domain.
key_novelty: Large models (70 billion parameters) retain general knowledge when specialized on astronomy with high-quality data, unlike smaller models, as shown by AstroLLaMA-2-70B outperforming previous astronomy-specialized variants.
contributions: Astronomy MCQ benchmark for objective evaluation of specialized LLMs in astronomy
AstroLLaMA-2-70B model achieving performance improvements through data-quality-focused continual pretraining
Empirical analysis showing model size mitigates catastrophic forgetting in domain specialization
Demonstration that high-quality domain-specific pretraining data partially recovers base model performance

metrics.accuracy: Performance on astronomy MCQ benchmark tasks

limitations: Catastrophic forgetting remains problematic in smaller models, and supervised fine-tuning dataset constraints limit instruct model performance.
